title: Enterprise Ask Synthesis and Account-Cohort Scoping
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a repeatable process and tooling to aggregate enterprise feature requests from Sales/CS, synthesize them into capability statements, and produce an initial engineering feasibility & cost bucket for prioritization. Deliverables: a synthesis template, scoring rubric, a sample consolidated request for top 3 accounts, and a CS handoff checklist.
background: We receive a steady stream of non-bug feature asks from Sales and Customer Success that are account-specific or variant requests of existing capabilities. Current intake is ad-hoc, causing duplication, unrealistic engineering asks, and low transparency for prioritization. This work aims to standardize the first-pass scoping so PM/Eng can quickly decide whether to accept, prototype, or decline requests at a per-account and cohort level.
scope_in: - Aggregate asks for a given timeframe (monthly)
scope_in_additional: - Produce a single synthesis artifact per account cohort and a prioritized list of top candidate asks
scope_out: - Implementation work beyond initial feasibility and cost buckets
acceptance_criteria: A reusable synthesis template that converts multiple Sales/CS requests into a concise capability statement (problem, desired behavior, value, signal)
A scoring rubric (effort, customer value, strategic alignment, technical risk, revenue proximity) with example scores for 10 historical asks
One consolidated sample scoping doc for top 3 customers in the "enterprise-gaming" cohort
CS handoff checklist and Slack/Confluence templates for request follow-up
Stakeholder review and sign-off from Eng lead (Rohit Patel) and Head of CS (Lena Ortiz)
notes_risks: Risk: consolidating asks can obscure unique regulatory or data residency requirements per account. Trade-off: grouping by cohort enables prioritization but may underrepresent a high-revenue single-account ask. Mitigation: include a high-revenue override flag and quick compliance checklist in the template.
